query: My friend keeps venting about the same things and just goes around in circles. Do I need to fix their problems?
ideal_answer: Not always. The author says that when it comes to loving other people, they mostly just want to be heard, and they ultimately need to feel seen. In the same way that witnessing what you feel seems to alchemize the feeling, you can offer that to other people by witnessing them. They do not always need you to solve a problem, interject, or have a well thought out response. Sometimes all they really need is someone to sit quietly with them and listen, even when their words are messy, going in circles, and unsure of what they are really trying to say. Sometimes all anyone really needs is someone who sees.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Everything in my life feels on pause right now. Is that a bad sign?
ideal_answer: No, the author says it usually is not. You may fear the quiet times in your life, when your soul goes through a winter, but it is often in those same times that the most profound and human work of all is being completed. Be still and do nothing. It is both the quiet and the noise that writes the symphony, the blank canvas and the paint that makes the picture, the rest and the movement that gives you the wisdom, insight, and clarity to press forward more boldly than ever before. When it feels like nothing is happening, that is when everything is about to happen, and you should not get so used to chaos that peace feels like something is wrong. The space between no longer and not yet is what defines the pivot periods of our lives. It is a time when you have nothing left to hold onto but also nowhere clearly to land, and most people revert to their oldest and most familiar coping mechanisms, confusing what is known for what is right. If you find the courage to hold your heart open through this, you create an opportunity for miracles to find you, take root in you, and change you through and through. If you find the resilience to make peace with the unknown, to not require every answer to keep moving forward, and to believe everything will work out one way or another, you begin to live more completely in the moment. One of the characteristics of having a big destiny is that things do not work out right away, and there are delays and unexpected times of quiet. These rest periods are life's way of giving you an opportunity to work on yourself, to invest in who you want to be, to heal, and to release. They are not just to be tolerated or waited through, but used, and they are quiet gifts that will lead you to the path you were really meant to be on. Your energy will return and your love for life will pour out of you again. You are not meant to be forever in an exhale, an expansion, a flow; some periods are intended for taking it in, for contracting and clearing, for ebbing, and for learning something vital through them. You are not meant to be flowering all of the time, and that is precisely what makes it so sacred when you do. One day you will look back on this time and understand the purpose in the timing and the delays, realize you were far closer to the breakthrough than you knew, and see that you were always right where you were meant to be.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: If I've made mistakes in the past but I'm really changing now, will people eventually forgive me?
ideal_answer: Often, yes. The author says you would be surprised how much of the past can be forgiven and forgotten if consistently different behavior is displayed in the now.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Do I have to travel the world or take big risks to really live a full life?
ideal_answer: No. The author says you may believe that living life to the fullest is seeing every country in the world, quitting your job on a whim, and falling recklessly in love, but it is really just knowing how to be where your feet are. It is learning how to take care of yourself, how to make a home within your own skin, and how to build a simple life you are proud of. A life most fully lived is not always composed of the things that rock you awake, but of those that slowly assure you it is okay to slow down: that you do not always have to prove yourself, that you do not need to fight forever or constantly want more, and that it is okay for things to be just as they are. Life can only grow outward in proportion to how stable it is inward, so if the joy is not in the little things first, the big things will not fully find you. If you understand that life is about the little things, you will never find yourself wanting more than what is in front of you. True joy is using what you have, being where you are, and loving the souls who have chosen to walk with you, and the desire for grandiosity is a projection of the lack of true depth you feel within. It is okay to want a quiet kind of life, one that is biggest within the little things, and an easy kind of life, filled not so much with reaching as with simply placing your hand down on all that is in front of you right now. It is a life where you move at your own pace, create in your own time, and hope your legacy will be one of a constant, loving presence that reminded others of how much goodness can exist within a human soul. To be truly alive is, in many ways, to embody a slowness of living: to stretch and savor the precious little things, to create pockets of calm out of ordinary hours and be in them completely, and to focus more intently on what is in front of you without your mind wandering to what is not. It is the capacity to lean into the experiences you are given, realizing they are not all good nor bad, though a warped mindset can make them seem so. You change as you shift your attention, redirecting your focus toward the parallel realities you are one thought away from living.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Is it okay to outgrow things and people I still love, or does that mean I'm failing?
ideal_answer: Yes, it is okay, and the author says it is not a failure. You will have to learn how to outgrow some things you love, and that some things are right for a time, but not forever. Moving on from them does not diminish the place they held within you, the importance they have to you, or the impact they had on you. If you are not growing, you are not really living, and if you are not moving on from anything, you are not moving toward something. You will have to learn how to let go of some things that are still beautiful, because you know they are not quite right and that a deeper peace is waiting. The people, places, and things that phase in and out of your life come to you for a specific purpose, and once their mission is complete, you are able to move on to the next experience. The very act of letting go is not a failure, but a signal of completion, one of the truest signs that you are evolving as a human being. Not every connection is meant to last forever, and the ending is not a failure. Sometimes it is a sign of completion, sometimes a sign of growth, sometimes a sign of beauty, and sometimes a sign of the truest love of all: the willingness to let someone chase the life that is calling to them.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: I don't know what my next step in life should be. How do I figure it out?
ideal_answer: The author says that if you do not know what to do next, it usually is not because your next step is far out in the distance, but because it is right in front of your feet. You are being asked to stop gazing outward and start looking inward, and you are being called to rebuild yourself at this exact moment. It is not because you need to seek more answers, but because you need to accept the ones you have already been given. It is time to learn to be in the answered prayer that is this very day, to use what you already have and be as you really are, to stop waiting for some future scenario to bring your dreams into the light, and instead to dig them out from beneath your fear and truly begin. To work out what to do next, ask yourself honestly what your 90-year-old self would advise you to do and what they would have wished you had done. Ask yourself honestly what you have sensed from the beginning, and what you have ignored, quieted, and distracted yourself from. Make two lists, the positives and the negatives, and weigh them. If there is one thing on the left that overpowers the dozen things on the right, trust that. Ask yourself what path will make you more of the person you are meant to be. If you do not yet know what choice to make, then it is probably not time to make it. There is probably another area of your life that is asking to be nurtured, developed, and strengthened instead. New factors in your decision making have not been introduced yet, because you do not know what you do not know, and you may be premeditating a decision that will need to be made eventually, but not today. When that day arrives, you will know what to do, because you spent this preparation period strengthening your sense of self and clarifying what you really want and what you really value in life. So give yourself space. If you are not certain, wait; time reveals all truth, all knowing, all reality that will come to be, and it will all become clear.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: What does it mean to take a leap of faith?
ideal_answer: The author says the leap of faith is when you step away from what is good in pursuit of what could be extraordinary.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: I feel lonely even when I'm surrounded by people. Why does that happen?
ideal_answer: The author says it can happen when you use irony and cynicism as shields, a way to laugh off your life so that it cannot truly touch you. This slowly ices you out of your own experience until one day you wake up and realize you are surrounded but lonely, busy but disengaged. If you want a full life, you have to be willing to open yourself to it: let it all in and let it move you, change you, free you, and make you feel again. Let what is heavy hurt and what is healing lighten, and move through it all without getting too attached. It is also entirely possible to find yourself in a crowd and feel deeply alone and not understood. What matters is not how many people you can surround yourself with at any given time, but how much time you spend with the ones who actually see you, who value and prioritize you, who feel like the family you have chosen. So the author says to prioritize the depth of your connections as opposed to the width of them.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Does loving myself mean ignoring my flaws?
ideal_answer: No. The author says that to see yourself lovingly does not mean glossing over your imperfections, the breaks within your being, or the ways in which you need to mend yourself from the inside and grow. It means to believe that you are capable of doing that healing, and that you are strong enough to keep going, not only to make it through another day or another week, but to leap in the direction of your desires. It means to know that you can trust your own steadiness, that you can endure your own storms, and that you can carry yourself through all the rest of your life.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Everyone around me seems to be ahead in life. Am I falling behind?
ideal_answer: The author says that just because something is not happening in the timing you expected does not mean it is not happening. Sometimes things do not unfold on your timeline because they are occurring on one that is far greater. Sometimes the things you would choose for yourself only rise to the level of your broken self-perception. Sometimes, when the light hits your eyes after staring for so long into the darkness, it is painful. Sometimes life is trying to give you more than you would ever take for yourself, and you should let it lead you higher than you would ever expect to go. The parts of your journey where you felt like you were failing and falling behind, the moments when it seemed like nothing was working out the way it should, and the times when you were all but forced to prioritize rest, begin self-reflection, or change were not your setbacks but your breakthroughs in disguise. The universe is constantly asking if you are ready to stop engaging with your old habits and enter a parallel life, one you begin to build in the gaps between what happens and how you respond. The next time you face the exact same challenge, you are being called to ask: how can I respond differently this time? Sometimes your hardest pivots are rerouting you to your greatest destinies, and you are growing through the most unlikely and confusing circumstances. Sometimes, when it seems like you are falling behind with the outside world, you are actually coming into alignment with your internal one, finally listening to the deeper inner wisdom that is telling you that you are meant to move beyond everything you have known into something bigger than you have ever fully let yourself believe.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: How do I make sure other people can't hold anything over me?
ideal_answer: The author says that if you promise yourself that they will not stop you, then they will be able to hold nothing over you.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Is it okay to start my life over from scratch?
ideal_answer: Yes, the author says it is okay. It is okay to disappear for a while to work on yourself, to disappear for a while and start over, and to wipe the slate clean and begin again. The world as it is today does not give us the grace for the normal transitions you are meant to go through, so you need to create space within your life to signify your internal growth and to mark for yourself the end of one chapter and the beginning of another. Maybe you are getting a second chance, another opportunity to clear the slate and begin again, and maybe the second part of your life begins after this crisis, and you will see the purpose in it all one day. It is okay to unearth the seeds you have planted when you realize your garden is not harvesting what you need to grow. It is okay to begin again, and to think differently, want differently, and move differently through this world. Your journey is defined by how you tell the story and by how willing you are to tell a new one when it is time. All change, no matter how minor, requires a period of reacclimation, because your entire being has to get used to functioning within a new frequency, a new dimension you have entered whether you realize it or not. Your journey will be filled with new beginnings, so when you arrive, embrace them and rest in them. Wash your past clean and start over; let go, let go, let go, and relearn life from this new vantage point and this new storyline. Let yourself leap into the newness in front of you, and keep leaping until you have carved out a sense of home from the once complete unknown. The author hopes you find the courage to change course as often as you need to and never let your ego keep you on a path you know is not right for you. Life was never meant to move in straight lines, and most of us are too scared to admit that what we spent so much time constructing around us was built with fragments of foreign, unfamiliar dreams. It takes a lot of heart to release it all into the nothingness and begin again, building a life that is specifically, simply, and perfectly your own.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: Why do I keep repeating the same patterns even when I know they hurt me?
ideal_answer: The author says your brain works against you in ways you do not realize. The compulsion to repeat makes familiar discomfort desirable, and the negative is disproportionately focused on because it feels like a more clear potential threat. You are an evolving being trying to operate with pieces of a machine developed for the most blunt kind of survival. Most people never realize how deeply the compulsion to repeat can run, or how entrenched we can become in the paths we have walked over and over again, until we cannot see anything beyond them. When you live from what is immediately comfortable, you miss out on what is infinitely beautiful, what exists beyond where the limits appear to be. It takes strength to witness your own patterns and correct your course, and to resist what has become so familiar. Your growth is the product of witnessing those impulses and choosing otherwise, again and again, until it is instinctive, until it is rewired. It takes strength to choose differently, to believe in what you can sense but not yet see, to be different, to be humble, and to change, and to become the person you have always wanted to be.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: I feel like I'm full of contradictions. Is something wrong with me?
ideal_answer: No, according to the author this is simply what you are. You are a field of contradictions, a constellation of experiences both painful and gorgeous, and all of the lingering hurts and shining possibilities that glisten in between. You might want to define yourself by the most knowable parts, the cleanest and clearest self-concept imaginable, but the journey of true self-actualization is to embrace your juxtapositions. It is to hold them up to one another and understand that it is not always comfortable to consider the aspects of ourselves that complement and contradict each other, the pieces that do not fit and do not make sense. But coming to grips with them is how you become the fullest version of yourself, and it is how you set your entire life free.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be

query: I avoid confrontation and anything uncomfortable to keep my life peaceful. Is that a good way to live?
ideal_answer: No, the author says avoiding discomfort is not the measure of a well-lived life. The measure of a life well-lived is not how often you have avoided discomfort, pressure, or change, but the grace with which you navigated it. To say that you faced not even a fraction of resistance within your life proves nothing more than that you were defined by nothing: you tried for nothing, stood for nothing, and did nothing with the gifts that were given to you. It may seem like the absolute worst thing in the world is to be disapproved of, but the actual worst thing is to paralyze yourself under the guise that you might be able to avoid any friction. The merit is not in whether or not you have ever experienced anything challenging, but in the courage with which you faced what challenged you. That is what matters, and that is what defines who you are.
source: The Pivot Year: 365 Days To Become The Person You Truly Want To Be
